hypotheses.question: Which physical invariants should a fluid discretization preserve, and what changes when it does?
hypotheses.connection: Geometric mechanics offers a route from symmetry and variational principles to fluid algorithms that preserve selected discrete structure.
hypotheses.entry_point: Compare circulation and energy behavior on a small inviscid-flow example; distinguish exact invariants from good long-term energy behavior.
hypotheses.falsification: Deprioritize if conservation diagnostics and geometric methods are not useful to the user's actual fluid questions; this is not automatically a viscous Navier–Stokes solver.

reference.title: Structure-Preserving Discretization of Incompressible Fluids
reference.scope: Author abstract: variational discretization of Euler fluids and a discrete circulation theorem; not a claim about every invariant or viscous flow.

hypotheses.question: Can a linearly stable model still strongly amplify disturbances before they decay?
hypotheses.connection: Robust-control sensitivity and non-normal linear dynamics meet in transient growth, resolvent analysis and pseudospectra.
hypotheses.entry_point: Start with a two-by-two non-normal matrix; compare eigenvalues with finite-time disturbance amplification before examining a fluid operator.
hypotheses.falsification: Deprioritize if the relevant operators are effectively normal or finite-time disturbance growth is not an active concern; linear amplification alone does not prove nonlinear transition.

reference.title: Hydrodynamic Stability Without Eigenvalues
reference.scope: Author-hosted paper: nonmodal amplification in shear flows can matter even with decaying eigenmodes.

hypotheses.question: Which assumptions let a noisy measurement support a reliable reconstruction?
hypotheses.connection: Instrumentation, information and Fourier methods suggest inverse problems and sparse recovery as bridges to imaging and audio.
hypotheses.entry_point: Reconstruct a small synthetic signal from noisy or incomplete measurements, then test sensitivity to sparsity and measurement assumptions.
hypotheses.falsification: Deprioritize sparse recovery where the signal/model is not sufficiently sparse or the sensing assumptions fail; the book biography does not establish this technical preference.

reference.title: Stable Signal Recovery from Incomplete and Inaccurate Measurements
reference.scope: Author abstract: recovery guarantees under specified sparsity and measurement conditions; application to a particular image or musical signal remains a hypothesis.

hypotheses.question: Can computational geodesics and tensor calculations make geometric physics easier to explore and verify?
hypotheses.connection: Relativity and manifold methods can be explored through symbolic curvature calculations and numerical trajectories, with coordinate and conservation checks.
hypotheses.entry_point: Use a familiar metric for a small geodesic visualization and verify a known limit before moving toward Kerr geometry.
hypotheses.falsification: Deprioritize if the interest is primarily axiomatic/analytic rather than computational; a convincing picture is not a correctness proof.

reference.title: EinsteinPy project
reference.scope: Official project page describes geodesic trajectories, symbolic tensor calculations and visualization; suitability and numerical validation remain to be assessed.

hypotheses.question: How should structures, uncertainty and control be designed together rather than optimized separately?
hypotheses.connection: Materials, sensing and feedback suggest coupled structural/control and thermal design studies, potentially including aerospace applications.
hypotheses.entry_point: Begin with a small mass/stiffness/control tradeoff; establish whether the composite-materials book is relevant before making aerospace-specific assumptions.
hypotheses.falsification: Treat as tentative until the materials title/purpose and an actual coupled-design question are confirmed; do not infer a current aerospace priority from the shelf.

reference.title: OpenMDAO project
reference.scope: Official project page gives multidisciplinary optimization, aerostructural and cubesat examples; no claim that it validates a specific composite design.

hypotheses.question: Which small algebraic foundations could be formalized before attempting machinery from vertex operator algebras?
hypotheses.connection: Representation theory and graded algebra offer possible stepping stones toward computer-checked mathematical structure.
hypotheses.entry_point: Survey graded-algebra and representation primitives, then choose one small identity or construction to formalize with explicit definitions.
hypotheses.falsification: Deprioritize if formalization is not useful to the user's algebra questions; existing graded-algebra infrastructure is not evidence that vertex operator algebra or the Monster construction is already formalized.

reference.title: Mathlib graded-algebra documentation
reference.scope: Official library documentation defines internally graded algebra structures; the bridge to VOA formalization is an exploratory proposal.
